notes: The 72-hour Leap Visitor Card costs 16 EUR (bus, DART, Luas); for the airport, take the 747 Aircoach. The city is walkable: take the DART to Howth, St Kevin's Bus to Glendalough and a tour to Moher.
Summer brings 15-20°C, changeable weather and light until 22:00. A rain jacket is essential for the cliffs and Howth; August is crowded.
A pint costs 6-9 EUR (Temple Bar 9+), fish and chips 12-15, a pub lunch 15-20. Tip 10% in restaurants, nothing in pubs.
Book of Kells and Guinness need timed online tickets; Kilmainham Gaol tickets sell out months ahead.
For traditional music try The Cobblestone or O'Donoghue's; Temple Bar is touristy and expensive.
The Cliffs of Moher day lasts 12 hours; the journey is tiring, but the views are Ireland's best.

stops.name: Trinity College Book of Kells
stops.tips: A 9th-century manuscript and the Long Room library; book online for 10:00.

stops.name: Grafton Street
stops.tips: Pedestrianised shopping street with buskers and Bewley's café.

stops.name: St Stephen's Green
stops.tips: Victorian park with ducks and a bust of Joyce.

stops.name: The Pig's Ear Dublin
stops.tips: Modern Irish cooking opposite Trinity; try the lunch menu.

stops.name: Temple Bar
stops.tips: Cobbled pub quarter. The Temple Bar pub is touristy (pint 9 EUR); Palace Bar is where locals go.

backups.name: The Stag's Head
backups.tips: Victorian pub dating from 1895, with Guinness and live music.

backups.name: Dublin Castle
backups.tips: Castle and the Chester Beatty Library (free); an alternative to Grafton Street.

stops.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
stops.tips: Ireland's largest cathedral, with Swift's grave.

stops.name: Guinness Storehouse
stops.tips: Seven-storey beer museum; a free pint and city views at the Gravity Bar. Book online (26-33 EUR).

stops.name: The Liberties Teeling Whiskey Distillery
stops.tips: Distillery tour and tasting in the heart of the city.

stops.name: Leo Burdock Fish and Chips
stops.tips: Dublin's fish and chips address since 1913, near Christchurch.

stops.name: Christ Church Cathedral
stops.tips: Viking-era cathedral and crypt (with a mummified cat and mouse).

backups.name: The Brazen Head
backups.tips: Ireland's oldest pub (1198); order the Irish stew.

backups.name: Kilmainham Gaol
backups.tips: Prison of the 1916 Rising; guided tour only, book online months ahead.

stops.name: Howth Cliff Walk
stops.tips: 30 minutes by DART; the 6 km Bog of Frogs loop passes a lighthouse and seals.

stops.name: Howth Market
stops.tips: Weekend market with crafts and food stalls.

stops.name: Beshoff Bros Howth
stops.tips: Fish and chips by the harbour; family-run since 1913.

stops.name: Howth Harbour Seal Watching
stops.tips: Seals and fishing boats at the harbour pier.

stops.name: Howth Castle Rhododendron Gardens
stops.tips: In flower in May and June; a pleasant park walk in other months.

backups.name: Aqua Restaurant Howth
backups.tips: Seafood at the end of the pier.

backups.name: Ireland's Eye Boat Trip
backups.tips: Boat to the bird island; summer only.

stops.name: Glendalough Monastic Site
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from Dublin (St Kevin's Bus); 6th-century monastery and round tower, free.

stops.name: Glendalough Upper Lake Walk
stops.tips: Forest and mining-village trail between the two lakes; the Spinc route takes 3 hours.

stops.name: Wicklow Heather Restaurant Laragh
stops.tips: Pub-restaurant in Laragh with Irish stew and a whiskey library.

stops.name: Sally Gap & Lough Tay
stops.tips: Views of the Guinness Lake; go by car or tour, and see the PS I Love You bridge.

backups.name: Powerscourt Estate
backups.tips: Some of Ireland's finest gardens, plus a waterfall; an alternative to Sally Gap.

backups.name: Glendalough Hotel Bar
backups.tips: Pub lunch next to the monastery.

days.theme: North Dublin: museum and Phoenix Park

stops.name: National Museum of Ireland Archaeology
stops.tips: Celtic gold and bog bodies; free, on Kildare Street.

stops.name: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
stops.tips: Interactive emigration museum in the CHQ building.

stops.name: Urbanity Coffee
stops.tips: Roastery café in Smithfield; good for brunch.

stops.name: Phoenix Park
stops.tips: One of Europe's largest city parks, with deer, the Papal Cross and bike hire.

stops.name: Jameson Distillery Bow St.
stops.tips: Whiskey tasting tour in Smithfield.

backups.name: The Cobblestone Smithfield
backups.tips: Traditional music pub with a live session every evening.

backups.name: Dublin Zoo
backups.tips: Inside Phoenix Park; an alternative to the park itself.

stops.name: Cliffs of Moher
stops.tips: Day tour from Dublin (about 60 EUR, 3 hours each way); 214 m cliffs and O'Brien's Tower. Windy, so book online.

stops.name: Cliffs of Moher Visitor Centre Café
stops.tips: Visitor centre café with soup and soda bread.

stops.name: The Burren
stops.tips: Limestone moonscape with the Poulnabrone dolmen, on the tour route.

stops.name: Galway Latin Quarter
stops.tips: 1 hour in Galway on the way back; buskers and the pubs of Quay Street.

backups.name: Doolin Gus O'Connor's Pub
backups.tips: Music pub in the village below the cliffs; included on the Doolin tour.

backups.name: Kilkenny & Rock of Cashel
backups.tips: Alternative southern tour: a medieval city and a rock-top fortress.

stops.name: Merrion Square
stops.tips: Georgian doors and the Oscar Wilde statue.

stops.name: National Gallery of Ireland
stops.tips: Caravaggio and Vermeer; free.

stops.name: Bewley's Grafton Street
stops.tips: Café from 1927 with Harry Clarke stained glass; ideal for a farewell breakfast.

stops.name: Ha'penny Bridge
stops.tips: Iron bridge over the Liffey; the 747 airport bus from O'Connell Street takes 30 minutes.

backups.name: The Winding Stair
backups.tips: Restaurant above a bookshop, overlooking the Liffey.

backups.name: Little Museum of Dublin
backups.tips: City museum on Stephen's Green; an alternative to the gallery.
